title: private-deploy-scratchpad-olivia-2026-03-06
content:
Daily scratchpad — Private deploy field notes (VPC / on-prem)
Owner: Olivia Sun
Context: prepping for AcmeCorp pilot (air-gapped cluster with on-prem object store). Quick notes for on-site runbook and followups.

TOPLINE
- Rough install checklist working, but hit two blockers: customer firewall blocks outbound to control plane IPs; and HSM/KMS integration hasn't been validated with their vendor (Thales).
- Need final decisions on certs: use customer wildcard + internal CA for control plane, or bring our certs via VPN?

INSTALL STEPS (working draft)
1) Pre-reqs on customer side:
   - k8s v1.26+ cluster (tested on 1.26/1.27). Confirm node OS (Ubuntu 22.04 preferred).
   - GPU nodes: NVIDIA drivers >=535 + CUDA 12.1. Check nvidia-smi output on each node.
   - Storage: NFS mount at /mnt/models (or S3-compatible endpoint). If S3, need endpoint URL, region, access key + secret in vault.
   - DNS: wildcard for *.redwood-acme.internal pointing to internal LB.
   - Firewall: allow outbound TCP 443 to control-plane.redwood.ai (IPs: TBD) OR open VPN tunnel to control plane.

2) Cluster prep (commands to run)
   - kubeconfig: verify admin context (kubectl config current-context)
   - Install cert-manager (v1.15.0)
   - Install ingress controller (nginx-ingress or alb depending on env)
   - Create namespaces: redwood-system, redwood-control, redwood-models

3) Helm deploy (private-deploy-helm)
   - values.yaml: set storage.backend = s3|nfs, set tls.source = "customer"|"redwood", set routing.mode = private
   - set nodeSelectors for gpu nodes: "hardware-type": "gpu"
   - taints/tolerations: add tolerations for redwood:gpu=true if customer uses taints

4) KMS/HSM integration
   - Customer uses Thales Luna HSM. We need: client cert, PKCS#11 config, network reachability from control plane component to HSM mgmt port.
   - TODO: schedule call with security (Priya) + customer security to validate PKCS#11 plugin (action: Priya, due 2026-03-09).

BLOCKERS / OPEN QUESTIONS
- Outbound IPs for control plane: customer firewall team needs concrete IP list and FQDN. Action: ask infra to publish static egress IPs for hosted control plane (Riley).
- CA strategy: if customer refuses external certs, we must accept their CA bundle. Need a short doc on how to install their CA into our control plane pods at deploy time.
- Object store compatibility: Acme uses an S3-compatible endpoint with path-style buckets and self-signed TLS. Need to validate minio client settings and set skip_tls_verify = true in values. Potential security sign-off issue.

QUICK REMINDERS / FRAGILE STEPS
- SELinux: if enabled on nodes, make sure model volume permissions are correct (chcon -Rt container_file_t /mnt/models).
- systemd logrotate: models can be large, ensure kubelet eviction thresholds and pod ephemeral-storage limits set.
- GPU driver mismatch will cause ML runtime errors; run a quick smoke: docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi

SMOKE TESTS AFTER DEPLOY
- curl -k https://control-plane.internal/healthz (should return 200)
- kubectl -n redwood-system get pods -> all should be Running/Ready
- run a short inference job against local model: curl -X POST https://local-ingress/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

ACTION ITEMS (owners)
- Riley: get static egress IPs + publish to customer firewall team (due 2026-03-08)
- Priya: coordinate HSM cert exchange and PKCS#11 validation (due 2026-03-09)
- Olivia (me): prepare runbook for on-site engineer (include cmds above + checklist) (due 2026-03-07)

LINKS / REFERENCES
- Runbook (confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/123456789/Private+Deploy+Runbook
- Jira pilot ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PRIVDEP-412
- Helm chart PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-helm/pull/98
- Slack thread (customer setup): https://slack-redwoodworkspace/archives/C01234567/p1649951234567

NOTES TO SELF
- Bring printed checklist for on-site (hardcopy helps when VPN flaky).
- Record video of the smoke test steps for handoff to customer ops.
- Keep answers to firewall + cert questions concise for customer security team — they want minimal inbound openings.

END.
